decisions.statement: A seat short of a persona is written as no page.
A seat short of a domain is written as no page.
A seat short of a role is written as no page.
A seat short of a principal is written as no page.
A seat whose principal is no person names the seat above itself.
A persona, a role, a person and a seat above are named by page type and slug.
An assignment is addressed under the first page type with its slug.
A slug no page type has is addressed as a domain.
An assignment naming a page type that has its slug is not addressed again.
A slug two page types carry cannot be addressed from the slug alone.
An assignment the page addresses keeps the page type that page names.
An assignment addressing another slug than the seat states is addressed again.
The address a seat's page has is read from that page rather than composed.
The seat page type is reached by the id it keeps rather than by its slug.
The type a seat's page names is imported from the file the page type states.
A seat whose page type the index names no file for is written as no page.
A page written here imports its type from somewhere rather than from nowhere.
A stop takes away the page an address is read from.
A seat states the address the seat last had as well as the slug.
The address a seat states is kept where the page with that address has gone.
A body matching the file the body would land in is not landed again.
A seat's page is landed by a program rather than by an agent.
The page goes in through the change adding a file.
A seat that stopped has its page taken away with the files beside that page.
A path the index files no page at has that page alone taken away.
That one refusal is the only refusal the page alone is taken away after.
The landing a page goes through is handed in.
A landing that committed before it refused names that commit in the refusal.
Where a seat's page sits is read from the one rule rather than spelled again.
Nothing here runs the akasha command as a process.
A page written over hands in the body read from it, and a new page hands in none.

definition: the page written for a seat out of what it states
